title: Reading the Spark UI: Jobs, Stages & the SQL Tab

scenes.heading: Reading the Spark UI: Jobs, Stages & the SQL Tab
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Reading the Spark UI: Jobs, Stages & the SQL Tab and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: The tabs that matter
scenes.narration: The Spark UI is your primary tool for diagnosing performance, and a few tabs do most of the work. The Jobs and Stages tabs show where wall-clock time is spent and which stages are slow. The SQL tab visualizes the physical plan with per-operator metrics, and the Storage and Executors tabs reveal caching effectiveness and per-executor imbalance.

scenes.heading: A diagnosis workflow
steps: Confirm the cause in the SQL tab
scenes.narration: A reliable workflow starts at the Jobs tab, drilling into the slow job and then the stage that dominates its runtime. Inside the stage, you examine the distribution of task times, because a large gap between the median and the max task exposes skew. You then look at shuffle read and write sizes and any spill to see if data movement is the bottleneck. Finally, the SQL tab ties the slow stage back to a specific operator in the plan.

scenes.heading: Healthy vs problem signals
scenes.narration: In a healthy stage, task durations cluster tightly, spill is minimal, and executors share the load evenly. Trouble shows up as a maximum task time far above the median, which signals data skew, or large disk spill, which signals memory pressure. If a single executor is doing most of the work, you likely have a skewed key or too few partitions. These patterns point you straight at the fix.

scenes.code:
spark = (SparkSession.builder
    .appName("diag")
    .config("spark.ui.port", "4040")
    .config("spark.eventLog.enabled", "true")
    .config("spark.eventLog.dir", "/tmp/spark-events")
    .getOrCreate())
# Live UI at http://<driver>:4040; history via the event log
scenes.heading: Enabling the UI and history
scenes.narration: The live UI is served on port four thousand forty of the driver while the application runs. Enabling the event log writes the same information to disk so the History Server can replay it after the job finishes. This matters because the live UI disappears when the driver exits, and post-mortem analysis is often when you most need the data. Pointing eventLog.dir at durable storage preserves those records.

scenes.heading: Metrics worth memorizing
items: GC Time — heap pressure / fat executors
scenes.narration: A handful of per-stage metrics answer most questions. Shuffle read and write bytes quantify how much data is moving, while spill columns reveal memory pressure. High GC time hints at oversized heaps or too much cached data, and a wide gap between median and max task time exposes skew.

scenes.text: Read the UI before you tune; measure the bottleneck, don't guess it.
scenes.narration: Nearly every real Spark optimization starts with the Stages and SQL tabs telling you exactly where time and data are going.
